dimensions.assessment: Affects private parties, litigants, and defendants involved in international contracts or foreign legal judgments affected by U.S. sanctions.
dimensions.evidence: no person (other than the United States or a person acting on behalf of the United States) may bring a civil action in Federal or State court

dimensions.assessment: Mandates the removal and dismissal of specified foreign judgment enforcement actions currently pending or filed in federal and state courts.
dimensions.evidence: an action to recognize or enforce a foreign judgment or foreign arbitral award described in subsection (a) may be removed by any defendant to the appropriate United States district court, which shall dismiss the action.

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state or imply specific federal spending or revenue effects.
Amends title 28, United States Code, to add a new section restricting civil court jurisdictions regarding foreign judgments.

dimensions.assessment: Applies permanently to civil actions pending on or after the date of enactment.

importance_detail.rationale: Prohibits private parties from bringing civil actions in U.S. courts to enforce certain foreign judgments or arbitral awards tied to U.S. sanctions, impacting pending and future legal actions nationwide.
